title: Infinitesimal points of a group scheme commute
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme and $G$ a group scheme over $S$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. Let $D=S[\varepsilon]$ be its dual-number thickening [def-sc-dual-numbers]. The kernel of restriction $G(D)\to G(S)$ along $\varepsilon=0$ is a commutative group with its inherited pointwise group law.

source.place: Lemma 33.16.2 proof: square-zero pushout and epsilon_i mapping to epsilon; local arbitrary-ring form and group-unit-law application written out here

proof.text: Let D=S[epsilon] over S, and take infinitesimal points v,w, so their restrictions along S to D are the group identity. On D times_S D consider F=(v after first projection)*(w after second projection) and H=(w after second projection)*(v after first projection). Their restrictions to the first axis are v*1 and 1*v, equal by the unit laws; their restrictions to the second axis are 1*w and w*1, likewise equal.

Apply lem-ag-dual-numbers-diagonal to F and H. Their restrictions to the diagonal are v*w and w*v, respectively, by the naturality of the product and group multiplication. Subtype extensionality gives commutativity in the kernel subgroup.
